newsitem.title: USA: White officer acquitted in death of black motorist.
newsitem.headline: White officer acquitted in death of black motorist.

text.p: An all-white jury acquitted a white police officer Wednesday in the suffocation death of black motorist Jonny Gammage, officials in the Allegheny County district attorney's office said.

Brentwood Patrolman John Vojtas was found not guilty of involuntary manslaughter in Gammage's death, Azizee Sams, executive assistant to District Attorney Bob Colville, said. The jury deliberated for two days before reaching their unanimous verdict.
Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy appealed for calm in the city at a news conference.

An angry group of black protestors tried to rip down an American flag hanging outside the courthouse after the verdict hit the streets. Vojtas, who wept when the verdict was read, was rushed from the courthouse surrounded by police officers.

"I thank God that this ordeal is over for me," he told reporters. "I hope police educated by this case can prevent this kind of accident from happening again." Vojtas has been a policeman for 16 years.
Defence attorney Jim Ecker said he received death threats at his office following the verdict. Two other officers charged with involuntary manslaughter in Gammage's death still face trials next year.

Gammage, 31, was the cousin and business partner of Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Ray Seals. He died along a roadside in October 1995 after a traffic stop while in the custody of five white police officers. Two of the officers were not charged.

The cause of death was listed as suffocation caused by compression to the neck and chest. The officers testified in a coroner's inquest that they had to restrain Gammage by holding him face-down on the ground after he became violent during a traffic stop.

The jury foreman, who spoke with reporters but did not want his name used, said the jurors did not feel the prosecution presented enough evidence for them to convict Vojtas. "There was reasonable doubt," he said.

In a telephone interview with cable news network MSNBC, Jean LeFlore, Gammage's girlfriend, wept and said the verdict was "a case of injustice." Speaking from her home in Syracuse, N.Y., she said, "This is the saddest thing that's ever happened to such a decent man like Jonny Gammage. (Vojtas) is a murderer and they're letting him walk the streets."
Brentwood Lt. Milton Mulholland and Baldwin Patrolman Michael Albert, the other officers charged in the case, face trial next year. Their first trial ended in a mistrial last month.

The incident began when Mulholland pulled Gammage over early in the morning of Oct. 12, 1995, for what he said was erratic driving. He said Gammage became violent after leaving his car as the other officers were arriving to provide backup.

Vojtas' defence attorneys said he was acting in self-defence when he held Gammage down, but prosecutors argued that Gammage's death was murder. An autopsy report showed no traces of drugs or alcohol in Gammage's bloodstream.
